ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is a nitrogen atom N⁺ with a positive charge, connected on the left to an R group; a double bond is drawn between nitrogen and the carbon above/on the right. There are also several curved arrows in the figure, as well as carbonyl/hydroxyl-related fragments on the right, but the question requires ignoring these arrows and only reading the core connection relationship. Then reason: according to the method sketch, the core skeleton is R–N⁺, and N and C are connected by a double bond, so write R as the wildcard *, write the positively charged nitrogen as [N+], write N=C as (=C) connected after nitrogen, obtaining the SMILES as *[N+](=C).

method.method_draft: Inspect the image while ignoring all curved arrows. Read the core transition-state connectivity as R–N⁺ with N double-bonded to C. Convert R to the SMILES wildcard `*`, encode the positively charged nitrogen as `[N+]`, and encode the N=C double bond as `(=C)` attached to nitrogen. This yields `*[N+](=C)`.
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：图中左侧是一个带正电荷的氮原子 N⁺，左边连着 R 基；氮与上方/右侧的碳之间画有双键。图中还有若干弯曲箭头，以及右侧的羰基/羟基相关片段，但题目要求忽略这些箭头，只读核心连接关系。再推理：按方法草图，核心骨架是 R–N⁺，并且 N 与 C 之间是双键，因此把 R 记为通配符 *，把带正电的氮写成 [N+], 把 N=C 写成 ( =C ) 连接在氮后面，得到 SMILES 为 *[N+](=C)。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct structure-to-SMILES route: read the static atom connectivity and formal charge from the drawing, then apply basic SMILES syntax. With only one target answer, this is the genuinely available primary method.
planner_metadata.image_role: Use the image to identify the non-arrow structural features: an R substituent attached to nitrogen, a formal positive charge on nitrogen, and a double bond from that nitrogen to a carbon atom. Curved arrows and proton-transfer annotations are deliberately ignored.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to know that the requested output is a SMILES expression and that arrows in the mechanism drawing should not be included as bonds or atoms.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: represent an unspecified R group as wildcard `*`; put a charged nitrogen in brackets as `[N+]`; represent a double bond to carbon as `=C`; and write the carbon double-bonded from nitrogen as a branch if following the `*-[N+]` connection.
